explanation: Buffer up to 2k values. Whenever the buffer reaches 2k, use nth_element to partition by descending order and retain only its largest k values. Perform one final selection and return the element of rank k−1.
timeComplexity: O(n) average time using linear-average nth_element on O(k)-sized batches every k new entries, plus one final O(k) selection; no worst-case-linear guarantee is claimed. Heap variants do n O(log(k+1)) updates; C++ instead amortizes average-linear partitioning across O(k) batches.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary buffer, including k=1: the buffer is pruned whenever it reaches 2k. Heap or buffer retains O(k) candidates, independent of the total stream length.

correctness: A value discarded below the largest k of an observed prefix can never enter the largest k after more values arrive. Thus pruning preserves all candidates for the final kth largest, including duplicate occurrences. The final nth_element puts the kth largest remaining value at index k−1, which is also the kth largest of the whole stream.
walkthrough: With [7,1,9,9,4] and k=3, all five values fit below the 2k threshold. Final descending selection puts the retained top values 9,9,7 before the lower values, and returns index 2, value 7. For a longer stream, every six buffered values are pruned back to three.
edgeCases: The stream must contain at least k values.
